summary: Nantucket Memorial Airport (ACK) is the primary gateway to Nantucket Island, located just south of the town of Nantucket in Massachusetts. The airport sits on a former military airfield and is one of the busiest seasonal airports in the United States, with traffic surging dramatically during summer months as visitors travel to the island's beaches and historic downtown. It serves as a critical lifeline year-round, providing essential connectivity for residents and emergency services.
faqs:
Q: How far is the airport from downtown Nantucket?
A: The airport is approximately 3 miles south of the town center, a quick 10-minute drive or taxi ride.

Q: Are there nonstop flights from major US cities?
A: Yes, ACK receives nonstop service from several East Coast hubs, including Boston, New York, and Washington, D.C., with frequent seasonal routes.

Q: Is the airport open year-round?
A: Yes, the airport operates year-round, though flight frequency and available routes are significantly reduced in the off-season.

Q: Does the airport have car rental services?
A: Yes, several major car rental agencies operate on-site, though booking well in advance is strongly recommended, especially during summer.
transport_tips: Taxis, rideshares, and rental cars are readily available curbside at the terminal. During peak summer weekends, expect longer wait times for ground transport, so consider arranging a pickup in advance. Many visitors also rent bicycles at the airport, as Nantucket is highly bike-friendly.
local_tip: If you're flying out on a clear summer day, request a window seat on the left side of the aircraft for spectacular aerial views of Nantucket's moors, lighthouses, and harbor as you depart.
